title: External wall insulation: maintenance and annual inspection
subtitle: Keeping an EWI render system watertight and performing well after installation
excerpt: External wall insulation sits exposed to rain, frost, UV, and impact. An annual inspection of the render coat, beads, and sills catches the small failures before they let water behind the insulation board and cause serious damage.
sourceNotes: INCA (Insulated Render and Cladding Association) maintenance guidance; BS 8414 fire testing guidance for EWI systems; NHBC Standards Chapter 6.9 on render systems; PAS 2035 whole-house retrofit guidance section on ongoing monitoring.

glossaryTerms.definition: An insulation system attached to the outside face of a wall, with an insulation board bonded and mechanically fixed to the masonry and covered with a render or cladding finish.
A metal or plastic edge trim fitted at corners, window reveals, and base details of an EWI system to protect the render edge and create a clean stopping point.

content.text: system is watertight only while the render coat and its detailing remain intact. The main failure modes are cracks at window reveals and base beads, impact damage at ground level, and silicone sealant shrinkage at junctions with windows and doors. An annual inspection in autumn, before the wet season, catches these early.
at the bottom of the system should be held clear of the ground by a minimum of 150 mm. Check for soil or mulch banked up against the base; pull it back if present.

Check the window sills. The render should stop behind the sill overhang, not butt up against it; water running off the sill should drip away from the face of the EWI. If the sill drip edge is missing or the render runs up to the sill, water can track back behind the system.

Inspect the corners. Hairline cracks at the corner bead are normal after the first year as the system settles. Cracks wider than 0.5 mm need filling with an EWI-compatible flexible filler before autumn rain.

Check all silicone sealant joints at window and door frames. Silicone typically lasts 10 to 15 years before it shrinks away from the frame. Press the sealant with a gloved finger; if it feels hard and has pulled from one side, replace the run before water gets behind it.

Look for impact damage at ground-floor level. The render coat at 1 to 1.5 m height is vulnerable to bin damage, bikes, and children. Shallow chips can be filled with a pigmented acrylic filler; deeper damage that goes through the reinforcement mesh needs a patch repair.

Look for efflorescence (white salt bloom) on the render surface. This is usually a sign of moisture moving through the render from behind. Investigate the source before repainting; painting over efflorescence masks the symptom.
Check any pipe penetrations through the EWI. The collar or flashing at every pipe should be sealed; check that the silicone or foam seal has not pulled away from the pipe.
Hairline cracks: fill with a flexible exterior acrylic filler. Apply with a finger, wipe smooth, allow to cure 24 hours before rain.

Sealant replacement: remove old sealant completely with a silicone remover tool. Prime the frame and render rebate with the sealant manufacturer's primer. Apply a neutral-cure silicone; tool smooth with a wet finger.

Algae growth: a light growth of green algae on a north-facing render is normal after several years. Clean with a dilute biocide wash (proprietary render cleaner or dilute sodium hypochlorite); do not use a pressure washer at close range as it can damage the render surface.
When to call the original installer

A drum-hollow sound when you tap the render (press your knuckles firmly against the surface) suggests the insulation board has debonded from the masonry behind. This needs a specialist repair, the hollow area must be mechanically fixed before water gets in. The same applies to any section of render that has blistered or bulged outward.

rows.symptom: Damp patch on internal wall below a window in the EWI section
rows.cause: Water tracking behind the EWI at the sill detail or through a failed sealant joint
rows.fix: Trace the entry point externally; raking out and resealing the sill and sealant joint usually resolves it. If the damp persists after the seal is replaced, arrange a specialist survey.

rows.symptom: Vertical crack running the full height of a wall panel
rows.cause: Thermal movement at an expansion joint that was omitted or too narrow in the original installation
rows.fix: Requires the installer to insert or reopen an expansion joint; do not fill with rigid filler as it will re-crack.

rows.symptom: Render coat turning green across a large area each year
rows.cause: North-facing elevation with poor air circulation; render surface holds moisture
rows.fix: Apply a biocide wash annually in spring; repainting with an anti-fungal masonry paint extends the clean interval to 3 to 5 years.
